lead_characters.name: Pat rick (ben)
lead_characters.hook: Ben reads like the physical center of the crew: a brawler with a wrestler's presence and an ex-criminal's instinct for trouble. He has the kind of rough authority that can carry action, comedy, and loyalty all at once, especially in a story where muscle and ego are part of the fun.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a showcase for an actor who can play force without losing charm — the kind of part that lets someone lean into physicality, comic intimidation, and wounded pride. It sits in the lane of a John C. Reilly-style bruised comic presence or a Walton Goggins-type volatility, where the character can be funny and dangerous in the same breath.

lead_characters.name: Billy (billy)
lead_characters.hook: Billy has built-in contradiction: a cop who is also an ex-criminal, which gives him instant tension and a morally slippery edge. That dual identity makes him a natural source of suspicion, improvisation, and comic unpredictability inside the crew.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: Actors love roles that let them play both sides of the badge, and Billy offers exactly that kind of push-pull. The part has the same kind of charged ambiguity that makes characters like Ray Velcoro in True Detective or a Michael Keaton-style compromised authority figure so watchable.

lead_characters.name: Alejandro (ally)
lead_characters.demographics: Male · 20s-40s · Dollar Tree worker · planner · ex-criminal
lead_characters.hook: Alejandro is the brain of the operation, but the Dollar Tree job keeps him grounded in a world that feels lived-in and unglamorous. That contrast — planner with a working-class day job — gives him a smart, underdog quality that can make the whole crew feel more human.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is a great part for an actor who can play intelligence with humility, not just slick competence. It has the same appeal as a Lakeith Stanfield or Paul Dano type of role in the sense that the character can be observant, funny, and quietly strategic without ever feeling generic.

lead_characters.name: Jerry (Jerry)
lead_characters.hook: Jerry is the comic pressure valve, but the stay-at-home dad angle makes him more than a punchline — he is the guy whose domestic life collides with criminal life in a way that can generate real warmth. He feels like the emotional wildcard of the group, someone whose family responsibilities make every bad decision funnier and more loaded.
lead_characters.why_actor_wants_this: This is the kind of role that lets an actor play embarrassment, tenderness, and timing in one package. It has the same showcase quality as a Jason Segel or Paul Rudd-style comic lead, or the grounded family-man energy of a Ben Schwartz performance when the material lets him stretch into sincerity.
